title: A resident executable self-model

donor_sources.observation: The registry associates callable names with source and cached AST descriptions; it does not establish a native executable self-model.

mechanism: Resident program cells bind actual executable entries to source, contracts, generations, and measured behavior.
challenge: Refuse a mismatched source/code pair and demonstrate two executable generations within one PID.

title: Versioned live function dispatch

donor_sources.observation: Registering transformed Python source replaces a named callable in a dictionary; the donor has no concurrent native generation protocol.

mechanism: Atomic generation dispatch with invocation leases and compare-and-swap activation.
challenge: Concurrent calls must finish entirely on the generation they acquired, while stale activations fail.

title: Typed mutable reasoning IR

donor_sources.observation: The donor parses and transforms Python ASTs and composes callables, but does not verify typed native control flow or effect compatibility.

mechanism: Verified typed IR with bounded control flow, native cells, evidence dependencies, and executable lowering.
challenge: Reject bad joins, invalid native signatures, and effects on a pure branch before execution.

title: Resumable VM generation switching

donor_sources.observation: The donor schedules dependency-ready calls and passes intermediate results; it has no resumable frame migration across program rewrites.

mechanism: Stable continuation labels and verified live-value maps permit switching suspended VM frames.
challenge: A suspended computation must resume on a new graph without repeating its completed effect.

title: Compile candidate C into a live native module

donor_sources.observation: The donor turns generated Python source into callable functions; the proposed extension compiles C into actual native code.

mechanism: Compile, inspect, evaluate, and activate a versioned native C entrypoint inside the resident process.
challenge: An actual compiled function must change resident execution without restart; malformed candidates never activate.

title: Generate and execute bounded machine code in memory

donor_sources.observation: The donor executes transformed Python source; it does not generate machine instructions or manage executable memory.

mechanism: Emit a small verified scorer directly into executable memory with platform-correct write/execute transitions.
challenge: Execute emitted instructions, then replace their generation in the same PID without a compiler or dlopen.

title: Native ABI, relocation, and import contracts

donor_sources.observation: The donor discovers Python functions and invokes them with kwargs; it does not establish machine-level ABI or import compatibility.

mechanism: Validate native candidate entrypoints and imports against a bounded host ABI before activation.
challenge: Reject incompatible layouts and relocations before any candidate initializer or function executes.

title: Safe reclamation of live native generations

donor_sources.observation: The donor stores function references in dictionaries and compositions; it does not handle native image reclamation during concurrent execution.

mechanism: Generation leases and quiescence reclaim old code only after all calls and continuations release it.
challenge: An old call survives activation and returns correctly; old code unloads only after its last reference drains.

title: Transactional migration of resident heap state

donor_sources.observation: The donor retains shared Python locals across executions but supplies no schema-versioned state migration or rollback transaction.

mechanism: Prepare and validate a new state graph, then atomically bind it to the matching code generation.
challenge: Migration failure leaves old state unchanged; successful migration never pairs new code with old layout.

title: Atomic activation of cooperating executable cells

donor_sources.observation: The donor composes named functions but updates registrations individually, without a transaction over interdependent executable versions.

mechanism: Bundle validation and atomic generation roots keep cooperating native cells on one compatible version set.
challenge: Concurrent callers observe either the complete old bundle or the complete new bundle, never mixed results.

title: Shadow native candidates with replayed observations

donor_sources.observation: The donor forwards dependency results and caches call outputs; it has no native shadow-execution contract preventing duplicate effects.

mechanism: Shadow native generations consume exact recorded observations while real effects execute once through the active path.
challenge: A shadow attempt to alter or repeat a recorded effect must stop; valid replay produces comparable native outputs.

title: Counterexample-guided native executable synthesis

donor_sources.observation: The donor can define and transform executable Python tools; it does not require an independent oracle or preserve counterexamples across revisions.

mechanism: Generate native candidates, execute independent oracles, minimize counterexamples, and admit only surviving implementations.
challenge: A candidate that memorizes visible examples must fail hidden cases; repaired code must execute in the resident process.

title: Resident rollback with a bounded behavioral watchdog

donor_sources.observation: The donor contains failed replicas and chooses a survivor; it does not roll back resident executable generations.

mechanism: Watchdog-monitored native generation activation with safe rollback of future dispatch and compatible state.
challenge: A behavioral regression triggers same-PID rollback while in-flight calls retain valid generation ownership.

title: Causal profiling mapped to executable versions

donor_sources.observation: The donor records per-operation calls, timing, and errors, but has no attribution to live native code generations or causal improvement experiments.

mechanism: Attribute native execution costs and verified outcomes to exact code versions and decision contexts.
challenge: Calls spanning a hot swap must remain attributed to their acquired generation, and pure delay must not look like quality gain.

title: Effect-aware executable composition

donor_sources.observation: The donor composes callables by forwarding values directly, without typed effect analysis or per-stage governance.

mechanism: Compose native cells and governed observations into typed programs whose optimizer respects effects and evidence.
challenge: Reject illegal reordering or duplicated effects while parallelizing truly independent pure stages.

title: Profile-driven native specialization

donor_sources.observation: The donor rewrites Python ASTs and chains functions but does not specialize native executable paths from measured runtime invariants.

mechanism: Partial evaluation creates guarded native specializations with correct deoptimization to the generic implementation.
challenge: An input violating specialization guards must execute the generic path and preserve exact semantics.

title: Verified ephemeral tools synthesized as native code

donor_sources.observation: The donor defines executable tools from source and lists them, but lacks independently verified native admission and DSCO capability enforcement.

mechanism: Synthesize a bounded native tool, qualify its contract, and expose it for governed use during the resident session.
challenge: A new native tool must solve unseen cases, and denied effects must remain denied through its dynamic dispatch.

title: Learn semantics-tested executable rewrite operators

donor_sources.observation: The donor has hand-authored AST rename and decorator operations; it does not learn reusable transformations from verified improvement pairs.

mechanism: Generalize successful code changes into guarded rewrite operators and promote them only after held-out equivalence checks.
challenge: A rewrite that improves training examples but changes hidden semantics must not enter the learned operator library.

title: An evolution curriculum that retains prior capabilities

donor_sources.observation: The donor invokes optimizers with a default substring-or-nonempty-answer metric; it does not protect previously acquired native capabilities during evolution.

mechanism: Evolve native implementations against staged tasks, held-out oracles, and retained capability constraints.
challenge: A candidate gaining a new task while regressing a required old capability must be rejected.

title: A closed-loop same-process native self-repair demonstration

donor_sources.observation: The donor asks an LM structured questions about progress and improvement; it does not rewrite and activate resident machine code.

mechanism: Observe a real defect, synthesize and qualify a native repair, activate it in the same PID, then roll back a later regression.
challenge: The full loop must change executed native bytes without exec and reject or roll back a deceptive later candidate.
